title: Round to FP8
goal:
FP8 tensors come from converting wider types (Section 2). Write `quantize(x, fmt)`, which rounds every float in the NumPy array `x` to the nearest value that the format `fmt` (`"e4m3"` or `"e5m2"`) can represent and returns the result as a `float64` array of the same shape.

Round to nearest, with ties going to the value whose mantissa is even. Values that exceed the maximum normal magnitude saturate to $\pm$ that maximum (Section 2). Values below the smallest normal number land on the subnormal grid. The starter gives the format parameters.
hints: In a binade $[2^e, 2^{e+1})$ the representable values are spaced $2^{e - m}$ apart, where $m$ is the number of mantissa bits. `np.frexp(a)` returns `(f, p)` with `a = f * 2**p` and `f` in `[0.5, 1)`, so $e = p - 1$.
Below the smallest normal exponent, `1 - bias`, the spacing stops shrinking. Clamp $e$ from below with `np.maximum` and the subnormals fall out.
`np.round` rounds half to even. Compute `np.round(a / spacing) * spacing`, then clip to the format maximum and put the sign back.
